caseno: Civil Revision Nos. 1792 of 1996 and 1793 of 1996.
lawyer:
No one --- For the Petitioners.  
Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate  --- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Sabur Alam & others ------ Petitioners 
Vs.
Jahanara Begum and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Rule in Civil Revision No. 1792 of 1996 issued at the instance of the defendants calls in question the judgment and decree dated 28-9-1985 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 221 of 1994 granting mandatory injunction reversing the Judgment and decree dated 19-5-1995 passed by the Assistant Judge, Savar Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 44 of 1989 refusing mandatory injunction. 

 2. Rule in Civil Revision No. 1793 of 1996 also issued at the instance of the said defendants calls in question the said judgment and decree dated 28-9-1995 passed by the said subordinate judge in title appeal No. 216 of 1994 affirming the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 17-5-1994 passed by the said Assistant Judge in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 44 of 1989 whereby the learned Assistant Judge declared easement right of the plaintiffs to use the pathway and granted permanent injunction against the defendants restraining them from creating any obstructions in the user of the said pathway by the plaintiffs. Since both the Rules have arisen out of the same judgment and decree they are heard and disposed of by this judgment. 

 6. Both the parties led oral and documentary evidence in support of their respective cases. The learned Assistant Judge having considered the evidence on record decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs declaring their easement right to the said pathway and granting permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the user of the said pathway by the plaintiffs. The learned Assistant Judge, however refused to grant any decree for mandatory injunction for removing or demolishing the alleged obstructions created by the defendants on the said pathway on the finding that the plaintiffs could not establish on evidence that the defendants had created any real obstruction by way of constructing any building or any structure on the said pathway preventing the plaintiffs from using the same. 

 7. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge, the defendants filed title appeal No. 216 of 1994 against declaration of easement right and granting of permanent injunction in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs, on the other hand, filed a cross appeal. Title Appeal No. 221 of 1994, against the said judgment and decree dated 19-5-1995 of the learned Assistant Judge for refusing a decree for mandatory injunction in their favour. 

 8. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-9-1995 allowed title appeal No. 221 of 1994 by granting mandatory injunction in favour of the which was hitherto refused by the learned Assistant Judge. The learned Subordinate Judge however, dismissed title appeal No. 216 of 1994 filed by the defendants affirming the judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge declaring the easement right and granting permanent injunction in favour of the plaintiffs. The defendants thus being aggrieved filed the aforesaid two revisional applications and obtained the Rules. 

 10. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite parties, supports the reasoning’s assigned in the judgment and decree dated 28-9-1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge in the aforesaid two appeals. 

 13. It is found that the plaintiffs have been able to prove that the said pathway is the only access to and from their house and they and their predecessor in interest have been using the said pathway for more than 20 years for the beneficial enjoyment of their land in CS plots Nos. 13 and 25. The courts below have therefore rightly decreed the suit in respect of easement right and permanent injunction. The impugned judgment and decree of the courts below to that extent being in accordance with law is affirmed. 

 14. With regard to the mandatory injunction, the learned Assistant Judge having found no satisfactory evidence that the defendant petitioners created any real obstruction, except construction of a safety tank refused to grant any decree for the same stating that construction of the said safety tank on the disputed pathway did not prevent the plaintiffs from using the same as it in reality created no obstruction. The learned Subordinate Judge however by the impugned judgment and decree granted mandatory injunction on the finding that the plaintiffs were able to prove by virtue of evidence of PWs, 1, 2 and 3, also other documentary evidence that the defendants created real obstructions in the user of the said pathway during the pendency of the suit constructing a building and a safety tank and, as such, the same were liable to be removed. 

 19. In view of the discussions made above, the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-9-1995 passed by the learned subordinate Judge insofar as it relates to granting a decree for mandatory injunction is liable to be set aside.
